Part 1 · The load list

How much power does the VPSA draw, and when?

Part 1 · the plan

Machine power from the simulator, not from the nameplate

  1. One line per consumerrated, absorbed, consumed
  2. Power over a cycletwo machines that never peak together
  3. Maximum demandkW and kVA the transformer must carry
  4. Motor marginrating against the model's peaks

VPSA-V1-EE-LL-001 · part 2

Three powers on every line

Rated

Motor nameplate from the EQL: K-100 200 kW, K-101 132 kW.

Absorbed

Shaft power from the model: JI-100 and JI-131 over a cycle.

Consumed

Absorbed ÷ efficiency: what the network supplies.

The two machines draw about 85 % of the mean demand; small loads are assumed.

Interactive · model run, last full cycle of the design point

K-100 and K-101 never peak together

Separate peaks add to 260.7 kW; together the machines never exceed 216.7 kW.

Efficiency, power factor and duty turn kW into kVA

The model gives shaft power; the transformer sees kVA.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Absorbed power comes from the model, not the nameplate.
  • The coincident peak, 216.7 kW, is below the sum of peaks, 260.7 kW.
  • Peak demand 319 kVA × 1.25 needs 400 kVA by load.
  • K-101 needs 160 kW or a clamp on PIC-133.

Part 2 · Starting and cables

What sets the transformer and the cable sizes?

Part 2 · the plan

The start, not the load, decides

  1. Two ways to startVSD ramp for K-100, DOL for K-101
  2. The voltage dipstarting kVA against the fault level
  3. Transformer size500 kVA keeps the dip under 10 %
  4. Cable sizeampacity, running drop, starting drop

EQL drivers · K-100 on a VSD, K-101 direct on line

One machine ramps up, the other takes a step

K-101 with seal-water separator V-104 · AI-generated illustration (Gemini)

  • K-100, VSD: starts near running current; no dip.
  • K-101, DOL: draws 6.5 × full-load current at pf 0.3 (assumed).
  • That inrush dips the 400 V bus for every other consumer.

Motor starting · step 1 of 2

The dip is the starting kVA against the fault level

The VSD hides K-100's start; K-101's inrush reaches the bus.

Motor starting · step 2 of 2 · K-101, 132 kW, 400 V, 500 kVA

A 132 kW direct-on-line start dips the bus 9.7 %

Previous slide$I_{FL}=P/(\sqrt3V\eta\cos\varphi),\ \ 1/S_{sc}=1/250+z/S_T,\ \ \text{dip}=S_{st}/(S_{sc}+S_{st})$
$I_{FL}=\dfrac{132\,000}{\sqrt3\times400\times0.958\times0.87}=228.6\ \text{A},\quad I_{LR}=1486\ \text{A}$IE3 data (assumed)
$S_{st}=\sqrt3\times400\times1486=1.029\ \text{MVA};\quad S_{sc}=\dfrac{1}{0.004+0.05/0.5}=9.62\ \text{MVA}$500 kVA, z 5 %
$\text{dip}=1.029/(9.62+1.029)=9.7\ \%$limit 10 % at the bus

At 400 kVA the same start dips 11.7 %.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • K-100 ramps on a VSD; K-101 starts direct on line.
  • The K-101 start dips the bus 9.7 % at 500 kVA, 11.7 % at 400.
  • The transformer is 500 kVA because of that start.
  • The K-101 cable is 185 mm², set by the starting drop.

Part 3 · Oxygen zones and UPS

Where is the air not air, and what must stay powered?

Part 3 · the plan

No fuel, but two atmosphere hazards

  1. Not a flammable areano fuel in any stream
  2. Oxygen-enriched zonesabove 23.5 % O2: keep equipment out
  3. Oxygen-deficient zonesbelow 19.5 % O2: a life-safety hazard
  4. Vent plumeshow far a vent stays off-air
  5. UPSwhat must survive a dip or a blackout

Area classification · IEC 60079-10-1

No fuel anywhere, so no Ex zones

Non-hazardous

Air, oxygen and nitrogen only; oil-free compressor; zeolite dust does not burn.

Enriched > 23.5 % O2

V-102 holds 96.0 % O2; its leaks and vents enrich the air.

Deficient < 19.5 % O2

V-103 holds 12.0 % O2; its vents can suffocate.

Compositions from the design point; thresholds are common industry values.

Above 23.5 % O2

In enriched air, distance protects; Ex certification does not

V-102 and the AT-124 analyzer house · AI-generated illustration (Gemini)

  • Cable sheaths, gaskets and clothing ignite easily.
  • Ex equipment is certified for normal air only.
  • Keep switchgear, motors and lights out.
  • Inside: low-energy, sealed, oil-free devices.

Below 19.5 % O2

A deficient zone harms people, not equipment

No warning

Nitrogen has no smell; nearly pure N2 can cause collapse within one or two breaths.

Where

V-103, the HV-136 vent, K-101 and the V-104 drain hub.

Controls

Vent high, ventilate, fixed O2 monitors, entry permits.

Interactive · the schedule A1–A7 of the document

Seven areas, three kinds of atmosphere

A2–A4 are enriched and A5–A6 deficient; only A1 and A7 are plain air.

The SIS trips by de-energising

Loss of power is safe; the UPS is for everything else

Monitors and analyzers protect people only while they are powered.

Safe without power

XVs fail closed, XV-127 opens.

Ride through a dip

A K-101 start must not drop the solenoids.

Keep AT-124 reading

It needs minutes to restabilise.

Keep O2 monitors alive

A blackout is when people walk in.

Interactive · the tab's eeUps()

A 3 kVA UPS and a 10 Ah battery cover 30 minutes

The UPS load is only 1463 W: control, trips, analyzers and monitors, never the machines.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • The unit is non-hazardous for flammable gas.
  • Enriched zones need distance; deficient zones need monitors.
  • The O2 vent plume is enriched for about 12.7 m.
  • A 3 kVA UPS keeps control, trips and monitors alive.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Take absorbed power and its timing from the model.

2

Size demand on the coincident peak, motors on the highest peak.

3

Check the largest direct-on-line start before fixing the transformer.

4

Keep electrical equipment out of oxygen-enriched zones.

5

Put on the UPS what must survive a dip, not the machines.
